headline: MGAT Alpha closed 9 trades this week for a net -$57.49 (22.22% win rate, 2 of 9) — every family that traded lost, with stop-losses doing almost all of the exiting. The book is still well ahead of its own hold-and-never-trade benchmark since launch (+2.12% against -16.65% for holding the same seven coins untouched), but that gap widened because the comparison basket fell harder, not because the book gained; the book itself lost money again this week. The call stays 'needs a change' — unchanged from last week, with the same lagging family still under its win-rate checkpoint.

counterfactual.reason: The shadow comparison book is void for this run: it could never close a position, so none of its figures measure anything.

hold_benchmark.basis: $8,000 split equally across the seven coins the book bought in its first two cycles on 2026-08-25, held untouched, no fees

llm_adviser: LLM adviser: observer only — logs what it would do, cannot affect a trade (settled from source 2026-09-22).
sample_caveat: 9 closed trades this week, 136 all-time against the 200-trade target (68%). All-time is past the ~30-trade floor where win rate and PnL become directional rather than unreadable.
paper_caveat: Alpha is paper — simulated fills, no slippage, no thin-liquidity exits, no can't-sell-into-dust. A clean logic result here is never a claim that the execution floor works; that claim belongs to the Beta rung alone.
integrity: No CLASS-A changes landed in this week's window — the latest health-log entry predates it — so this week is cleanly comparable to the week before it.

verdict.text: Needs a change, the same call as last week. Stop-losses did almost all of the exiting — 7 of 9 closes, each roughly $10 to $13 — with one real winner and one near-breakeven time-stop on a pegged token; without both, the week would have lost about $80. Several coins keep stopping out and then getting bought back days later with no visible cooldown, and two coins are currently held open by two different strategies at once, which looks like it may be adding to the losses, though that is not fully verified from this read. Sizing itself looks fine: ten of eleven opens and all nine closes used a measured beta rather than a guessed one. Against the hold-everything benchmark the book is still well ahead, but only because the comparison basket fell further this week — the book itself lost money too, so that gap is damage limitation, not an edge. One brief, already-cleared data-feed blip was the only fault; it does not explain the losses.
